disclaimer: These are illustrative, synthetic reference profiles built from well-known public staging systems (GOLD for COPD) and typical physiology ranges. They are NOT real patient records and are NOT individually cited the way the drug PK table requires. Treat them as placeholder data to unblock rendering and simulation, and replace with reviewed, cited values before any claim beyond a hackathon demo.

field_notes.fev1_pct_predicted: Forced expiratory volume in 1 second, as % of the value predicted for a healthy person of the same age/sex/height
field_notes.fev1_fvc_ratio: FEV1/FVC ratio; below ~0.70 after a bronchodilator is the standard marker of airflow obstruction
field_notes.spo2_exertion_pct: Blood oxygen saturation during moderate exertion
field_notes.tidal_volume_ml: Air moved per breath at rest
field_notes.dlco_pct_predicted: Diffusing capacity for carbon monoxide, a proxy for gas-exchange surface area, as % predicted
field_notes.airway_resistance_multiplier: Relative multiplier on baseline airway resistance used by the simulation (1.0 = healthy baseline)
field_notes.vq_mismatch_index: 0 to 1 scale; 0 = perfectly matched ventilation/perfusion, higher = more mismatch and wasted ventilation
field_notes.respiratory_drive_sensitivity: Relative sensitivity of the brainstem's breathing drive to CO2/O2 and to respiratory-depressant drugs (1.0 = normal; lower = blunted drive, e.g. chronic opioid use or severe COPD with CO2 retention)

profiles.label: Healthy adult, non-smoker
profiles.basis: Standard healthy-adult reference ranges used in respiratory physiology teaching material

profiles.label: Mild COPD, current smoker
profiles.basis: GOLD stage 1 defined as FEV1/FVC < 0.70 with FEV1 >= 80% predicted; other values are illustrative midpoints

profiles.label: Moderate COPD, long-term smoker
profiles.basis: GOLD stage 2 defined as FEV1/FVC < 0.70 with 50% <= FEV1 < 80% predicted

profiles.label: Severe COPD with emphysema, former heavy smoker
profiles.basis: GOLD stage 3 defined as FEV1/FVC < 0.70 with 30% <= FEV1 < 50% predicted; reduced DLCO reflects alveolar destruction in emphysema

profiles.label: Uncontrolled asthma, non-smoker
profiles.basis: Asthma is primarily reversible airway obstruction; DLCO is typically near-normal unlike COPD, which is the key distinguishing feature to encode

profiles.label: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, former smoker
profiles.basis: Fibrosis is a restrictive pattern: FEV1/FVC ratio is normal or high (unlike obstructive COPD/asthma) because both volumes fall together, while DLCO drops sharply from thickened alveolar walls
